title: cMCP GatewayClaim
description: TRACE profile envelope emitted by the cMCP Gateway TEE at session close. The 'trace' sub-object contains canonical TRACE v0.2 fields; 'gateway' contains cmcp-specific addenda.

cmcp_version.description: Version of the cMCP claim envelope format. 1.1 signs over RFC 8785 (JCS) and carries only observed TRACE fields; 1.0 signs over sorted-key JSON with ASCII escapes.

trace.description: Canonical TRACE v0.2 fields for this gateway session.

iat.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the claim was generated.

subject.description: SPIFFE URI identifying the gateway session.

data_class.description: Highest sensitivity classification reached during the session.

entries.description: 1.0 claims only; 1.1 carries it as gateway.transcript_entries. Privacy-preserving per-call view (#126): tool name, data class, and policy decision, derived from the audit chain. No raw parameters or response bodies.

model_id.description: Model identifier as used by the provider.

weights_digest.description: SHA-256 or SHA-384 digest of the model weights. Required for local/confidential-inference deployments.

aibom_uri.description: URI to SPDX 3.0 AI Profile or CycloneDX 1.7 ML-BOM for this model.

build_provenance.description: SLSA provenance for the workload (agent code + container image).

slsa_level.description: SLSA Build Level achieved. Level 0 = software-only (development/staging); Level 2 minimum for TRACE conformance; Level 3 for production mark.

digest.description: SHA-256 or SHA-384 digest of the container image or workload binary.

provenance_uri.description: URI to the SLSA provenance attestation on a Sigstore/Rekor or compatible log.

provenance_depth.description: Depth of supply-chain verification the issuer claims for this record. surface: digest matches the workload artifact and builder is in a trusted set. builder: all of surface, plus provenance_uri resolves, the SLSA attestation signature verifies, its subject matches digest, and its builder.id matches builder. transitive: all of builder, plus every entry in the SLSA materials / resolvedDependencies has a verifiable publisher attestation. Records omitting this field are treated as surface by verifiers, so existing records keep their meaning.

appraisal.description: Verifier's EAR appraisal of the evidence (draft-ietf-rats-ar4si).

verifier.description: URI identifying the verifier the record names for this appraisal. In a record signed only by its producer this is the producer's claim, not authenticated by that verifier.

policy_ref.description: URI to the appraisal policy used.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch seconds when the appraisal was produced.

provenance_depth_verified.description: Depth at which this verifier actually checked build_provenance, which is not necessarily the depth the issuer claimed. A verifier may downgrade when deeper evidence does not resolve, and records the lower depth rather than a failure of the higher one. A verifier does not record a depth higher than it executed.

method.description: The method this appraisal used. A closed set, for the reason section 3.1.1 gives origin.kind: a verifier keys on it. This version defines one value, re-execution, the result of re-running a record's reproducibility claim (section 3.1.4). appraisal.status is untouched by it: the outcome below is not folded into the EAR status.

re_execution.description: The re-execution result, attributed to the party that re-ran the function and named as appraisal.verifier. In a record signed only by its producer this attribution is the producer's report, not authenticated by the verifier. Spec section 3.1.4. Present exactly when method is re-execution.

outcome.description: reproduced: the re-run completed on the closure alone and the digest of its transcript equals transcript_digest. diverged: the re-run completed on the closure alone and the digests differ. not-attempted: a closure blob could not be resolved, code_identity could not be obtained, the function read beyond the closure, the re-run did not run to completion, or the verifier could not establish that the re-run used the closure alone. not-attempted is never reported as either of the other two: absent is not pass, and absent is not failure.

observed_digest.description: The verifier's digest of the transcript its re-run produced. Required when outcome is diverged, because divergence localises nothing by itself: producer tampering, a function that is not the deterministic one it is named as, and verifier drift are indistinguishable until a third party can compare transcripts.

reason.description: Why no outcome could be reported. Required when outcome is not-attempted: a named absence and a generic one are different findings, and this is where the finding is kept.

verifier_code_identity.description: Digest of the verifier's own implementation. Self-asserted and carrying no weight singly; a correlation key across results, since two verifiers at different implementations disagreeing over the same closure is verifier drift, and that reading is unavailable without it.

allOf.$comment: Divergence without the observed digest cannot be compared by anyone.
An inability to check is reported with its cause, never rounded to an outcome.

platform_measurement.description: Per-layer appraisal of the platform measurement, attributed to appraisal.verifier. In a record signed only by its producer this attribution is the producer's report. A member of appraisal in its own right, not an appraisal.method value, so it can sit next to a re-execution result. measurement must equal runtime.measurement, a cross-field rule the reference model enforces. Spec section 3.1.5.

measurement.description: The digest this appraisal is about. Must equal runtime.measurement: a result about another measurement is not about this record.

layers.description: Keyed by the platform's name for the layer; on tpm2, pcr: followed by a register number from 0 to 23 in decimal without leading zeros. A result naming no layer establishes nothing.

additionalProperties.description: One layer's outcome. Spec section 3.1.5. reason is required when outcome is not-established and absent when it is established.

outcome.description: established: the evidence establishes this layer. not-established: it does not, for the reason given; never reported as established, and a layer the result does not list is not established either.

reason.description: layer-not-measured: the layer holds no measurement, its value is the initial value or, on a TPM, a separator and nothing else. measured-not-appraised: the measurements replay to the quoted value and nothing in the evidence establishes that what ran was appraised before it ran. evidence-spans-multiple-boots: the evidence does not establish that the quote and the event log describe the same single boot, and the log does not replay to the quoted value.

allOf.$comment: A not-established layer carries its reason; an established one carries none.
Section 3.1.4: re_execution is present when method is re-execution and absent otherwise. Mirrors the cross-field check in the reference model.
Section 3.1.5, rule 5: a verifier that writes platform_measurement has performed an appraisal, so status is not none. Mirrors the check in the reference model.

gateway.description: cmcp-specific addenda outside the canonical TRACE spec.

sequence_number.description: Monotonically increasing claim counter for this gateway instance (AUDIT-005).

edges_represent.description: Meaning of recorded edges; temporal adjacency does not establish causality.

agent_identity.description: Optional Agent Manifest binding carried by issue #302. The runtime emits this only after the signed manifest, authenticated agent subject, policy hash, and catalog hash have been checked at session creation.

subject_source.description: Source of the authenticated_subject assertion. config means configured runtime input, svid means transport/mTLS SVID, and manifest-dev means dev-mode fallback from manifest.agent_id.

intent_hash.description: AARM R2: digest of the issuer-signed declared intent (agent-manifest spec 3.9). Absent when the bound manifest declares no intent.

agent_key_thumbprint.description: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of the agent's own signing key (#425), distinct from issuer_key_id. Only ever set when subject_source names a live-authenticated source.

enforcement_mode.description: The Agent Manifest binding's enforcement mode at session creation, distinct from trace.policy.enforcement_mode.

policy_signing.description: Optional. Present only where a policy signing key is pinned (CMCP_POLICY_SIGNING_KEY). key_id names the key the policy in force at claim time verified under; revoked_key_ids lists the policy signing keys this gateway process has revoked, in order. A key_id that appears in revoked_key_ids means the policy in force had lost its signer and tool calls were refused. Key ids are sha256 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

kill_switch_triggered.description: True when the kill switch stopped this session's agent identity. Later calls and sessions from the same identity are refused until an operator lifts the block.

kill_switch.description: The kill switch settings in force for this session, and what tripped it. Present only when the kill switch is enabled; absent means it was not armed.

trigger.description: deny_rate when the threshold was crossed, operator when an operator tripped it. Absent when the switch did not trip.

transcript_entries.description: 1.1: privacy-preserving per-call view (#126), kept outside the TRACE block.

trace_omitted.description: 1.1: the required TRACE fields this claim leaves out because the gateway did not observe them. Non-empty means trace is not a complete TRACE record.

signature.description: Base64url-encoded Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON body (all fields except this one): RFC 8785 for 1.1, sorted-key ASCII JSON for 1.0.
